sermon.title: The Holy Spirit’s Teaching Power 12/10/2017
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 1 Corinthians 2 and John 14 that only the Holy Spirit knows and reveals the things of God. The Spirit who was with the disciples would be in them, teaching all things and bringing Jesus’ words to remembrance. He illustrates with opened understanding, the Ethiopian eunuch, spiritual discernment beyond Hebrew and Greek, and Elisha’s servant seeing chariots of fire.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A congregant’s name is in the transcript only. Kept as spoken: the prophet in 2 Kings 6 is mostly called “Elijah” (it is Elisha) (28:33–31:52). Points to check: Khrushchev memorized the first five books of the Bible (2:00); Philip transported “25 to 30 miles”; Pentecost “15 different languages”. Sensitive content kept as spoken: Syria “still invading it today”; some who claim the Spirit “act like maniacs”; Pentecostals didn’t let the Spirit teach them, others “like a dead log”; no need to be raptured out; North Korea and Russia; “the writer was drunk” (mocking skeptics).

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Elisha prayed, and said, “LORD, I pray, open his eyes that he may see.” Then the LORD opened the eyes of the young man, and he saw. And behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

So when the Syrians came down to him, Elisha prayed to the LORD, and said, “Strike this people, I pray, with blindness.” And He struck them with blindness according to the word of Elisha. Now Elisha said to them, “This is not the way, nor is this the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek.” But he led them to Samaria. So it was, when they had come to Samaria, that Elisha said, “LORD, open the eyes of these men, that they may see.” And the LORD opened their eyes, and they saw; and there they were, inside Samaria! Now when the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, “My father, shall I kill them? Shall I kill them?” But he answered, “You shall not kill them. Would you kill those whom you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set food and water before them, that they may eat and drink and go to their master.” Then he prepared a great feast for them; and after they ate and drank, he sent them away and they went to their master. So the bands of Syrian raiders came no more into the land of Israel.
